$comment: Reconciliation manifest for the local CI gate. Read by scripts/check-ci-drift.mjs.
One entry per step in .github/workflows, keyed by '<workflow>::<job>::<step name>'.
hash   - content hash of the step (run/uses + with + env + if) when it was last
reconciled. The guard recomputes it; a mismatch fails the gate.
mirror - the local command asserted to cover this step, or null when exempt.
reason - why the mirror covers it, or why it cannot run locally. Required.
IMPORTANT: `mirror` is a HUMAN ASSERTION, not something the guard verifies. The
guard's job is to make sure that assertion is re-made whenever the CI step changes,
so the local gate cannot drift out of sync in silence. When a hash mismatch sends
you here, actually re-read the workflow step before bumping the hash.

quality-gate.yml::changes::Check whether.reason: The step inlines the fallback directly (same pattern as the other four gate workflows): if base-ref/scripts/ci-changed-paths.mjs exists, run it and pass its output/exit code straight through; otherwise print a loud [MISSING BASE CLASSIFIER] warning and resolve relevant=true, on a code path that never invokes the classifier. scripts/ci-gate-bootstrap.test.mjs parses this exact `run:` block from the real workflow file (not a restatement) and executes it directly against both cases for all gate workflows. The classifier's own decision logic remains covered by ci-changed-paths.test.mjs.

quality-gate.yml::changes::Checkout clas.reason: GitHub-only: checks out the classifier script (scripts/ci-changed-paths.mjs) from the pull request's base commit into base-ref/ rather than its own merge commit. This pins the classifier's SOURCE so an accidental or careless edit (a rename, a bad rebase) cannot silently change it — it is NOT a defense against a pull request that deliberately tries to bypass its own gates, since the `changes` job's YAML itself (including the invocation step) is read from the pull request's merge commit the same as everything else in this workflow; see #1022 for the honest framing and why that residual exposure is accepted. Locally the working tree already is the code under test, and there is no PR base/head distinction to reproduce.

quality-gate.yml::changes::Setup Node.reason: GitHub-only Node setup for PR gating. This repository's local checks already assume Node is available locally for scripts and format/lint tooling.

quality-gate.yml::gate::Check required j.reason: GitHub-only: this is the #1017 aggregate required-check step, which reads the needs context (via toJSON(needs)) across the workflow's other jobs. Round-4 review fix: the round-3 shape now additionally correlates skipped work with the classifier's own verdict — asserts needs.changes.result is exactly success, requires needs.changes.outputs.relevant to be exactly true or false (failing closed on absent/empty/malformed, since GitHub can omit an output entirely), allows skipped only when relevant is false, and requires success (not skipped) from every required job when relevant is true. Previously every skipped result passed unconditionally, so changes=success with an absent relevant output and every heavy job skipped reported green. scripts/ci-gate-aggregation.test.mjs extracts and executes this exact run: body (parsed from the real workflow, not restated) against every documented result combination plus every fail-open shape a reviewer found. That context only exists inside a GitHub Actions run, so this step itself stays GitHub-only/unmirrored locally.

quality-gate.yml::gate::Verify the requi.reason: GitHub-only: round-5 BLOCKER fix. Reads steps.check-required-jobs.outcome, which GitHub computes BEFORE continue-on-error is applied (only .conclusion is rewritten afterward), so a continue-on-error added to the required-jobs check step cannot mask this step's own view of whether that step actually succeeded. That `.outcome` context only exists inside a real Actions run, so this stays GitHub-only/unmirrored locally; scripts/check-ci-gate-structure.mjs pins that this exact step exists.

require-linked-issue.yml::require-linked.reason: Reads github.event.pull_request.body. At pre-push time there is no PR and therefore no body to check, so this gate is unreproducible locally by construction rather than by omission. The step gained a #1240 waiver that short-circuits to success for PR_AUTHOR == 'dependabot[bot]' (exact-login policy, not github.actor, not a label); the waiver's exact shape is guarded by scripts/require-linked-issue.test.mjs, which just ci-drift now runs, but the step itself (which reads the live PR body) stays a GitHub-only required check.

react-doctor.yml::react-doctor::Resolve.reason: GitHub-only: derives a single DIFF_BASE per event (pull_request -> origin/<base_ref>, merge_group -> the merge-group base sha, push -> github.event.before with a HEAD~1 fallback for a brand-new branch) so the Assert diff base is present step and --base cannot drift. The checkout uses fetch-depth: 0, so the resolved base is present locally without fetching.

react-doctor.yml::react-doctor::Assert d.reason: GitHub-only: asserts the per-event DIFF_BASE (resolved by the Resolve diff base step) is present in the fetch-depth:0 checkout via `git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${DIFF_BASE}^{commit}"`, failing loud if it is not so an unexamined run can never be reported green. Round 2 fix: replaces the old `git fetch --no-tags ${DIFF_BASE}` step that aborted CI because for a PR the resolved value is the local remote-tracking ref name `origin/<base>`, which `git fetch` does not accept as a `<remote> <ref>` position. Locally origin/develop is already present, and the fetch-depth:0 checkout means the base sha is present without fetching.
